title: Introduce Econ Juggler: tenant-aware microbatch scheduler and quant-plan exporter
author: Maya Chen
body: Motivation: Large tenants with spiky traffic expose a tradeoff between per-request latency and per-token cost. Existing policies apply coarse tenant defaults (batch size, cache TTL, quant profile) and rely on manual tuning. This PR introduces Econ Juggler: a tenant-scoped microbatch scheduler that opportunistically groups requests while exporting a compact quantization plan driven by observed unit economics. The goal is to reduce token cost without violating latency SLOs and to surface a deterministic plan operators can review and pin. Summary of changes: - Add scheduler core (src/scheduler/econ_juggler.py): lightweight event-driven microbatch loop, tenant budget window accounting, and slow-path fallback when latency budgets are tight. - Quant-plan exporter (cli/quant_plan_exporter.py): generates per-tenant candidate quant profiles with cost/latency delta estimates, emits JSON that the Console and the operator CLI can consume. - Planner API (webapp/api/quant_planner.py): HTTP endpoints for plan preview, plan pinning, and safe-rollout metadata. - Telemetry hooks (telemetry/econ_metrics.py): new histograms and counters (microbatch_size, quant_plan_savings_est, tenant_budget_slack) and end-to-end trace spans. - Database migration (migrations/2026_02_25_add_tenant_econ_profiles.sql): adds tenant_econ_profiles table with compact columns for plan fingerprints. - Tests and benchmarks (tests/test_econ_juggler.py, benchmark/econ_juggler_small_load.yaml): unit tests for correctness, integration test for latency fallbacks, and a small bench script used to generate the included performance snapshot. - Docs and examples (docs/econ_juggler.md, examples/quant-plan-preview.ipynb): quickstart and example exporter workflow. Key behaviors and safety: - Tenant-aware batching: Juggler uses per-tenant sliding windows (1s/10s) to decide whether to pool microbatches; it honors request-level latency hints and SLO budgets from the route config. - Latency-first fallback: when p99 headroom falls below configured threshold, Juggler disables microbatching for the affected tenant until recovery. - Deterministic quant planning: exporter produces ranked quant presets (e.g., fp16->q4_0, q4_0->q3_8) with conservative loss estimates derived from sampled eval runs. Plans include a safety fallback mapping to ensure graceful degradation. Benchmarks: - Lab setup: 2x A100-40GB serving nodes, model: llama-2-13b (optimized runtime), mixed traffic composed of small chat requests (mean tokens 48) and long-form generation (mean 420), tenant skewed at 40% of overall QPS. - Results (stable dev run): avg token cost reduction ~10.5% for the target tenant, median latency impact +2ms, p95 latency stayed within 1% of baseline after fallback logic. See benchmark snapshot in the commit list for raw numbers. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler implementation and unit tests - [x] Exporter CLI and API endpoints - [x] Metrics and tracing integrated - [x] Migration included and tested in CI - [x] Bench and docs included Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.features.econ_juggler (off by default). Initial rollout: enable for internal tenants only, run exporter in dry-run mode to collect candidate plans for 2 weeks, then enable plan application for a small canary group. Related: ENG-4532 (tenant batch tuning), ENG-4601 (quant-plan ergonomics).

review_comments: Aisha: Can you add a counter for number of times the greedy microbatcher gave up due to latency headroom? This is important for alerting.
Maya (reply): Added tenant_budget_slack and microbatch_giveup_count metrics in telemetry/econ_metrics.py. Also annotated trace spans where fallback is triggered.
Marco: The exporter format is compact but we should include a deterministic fingerprint for plan diffs. Also prefer a semantic version field on the exported JSON.
Maya (reply): Export now includes plan_fingerprint (sha1) and spec_version: 1. Commit b7f3c12.
Samir: CI flagged a lint error on the migration (unused import). Please fix and ensure alembic test runs locally.
Maya (reply): Fixed import and added a tiny migration test to tests/test_migrations.py
release_notes: Introduce Econ Juggler: tenant-aware microbatch scheduler and quant-plan exporter. Reduces per-tenant token cost with tenant-scoped microbatching and exports quantization plans for operator review. Feature is feature-flagged and off by default.
notes_for_qa: QA should validate fallback behavior by simulating p99 headroom loss scenario and asserting that microbatching is disabled for the tenant and metrics microbatch_giveup_count increments. Validate exported plan JSON schema (spec_version, plan_fingerprint, candidate_profiles, estimated_savings).
